paper_metadata.title: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization Approach for Incorporating Solvency Capital into Portfolio Optimization

experiments.description: Quadratic proxy-model training experiment for approximating the solvency capital requirement (SCR) using regression on real insurance portfolio data with 26 asset classes.

algorithm.variant: general least-squares regression for quadratic SCR proxy modeling
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained over 100 epochs; low validation error achieved

hyperparameters.basis_functions: all pairwise products x_i x_j, linear terms x_i, constant term

problem_formulation.objective_function: Fit f3,approx(x) = x^T P x + b^T x + c to the SCR objective f3(x) by minimizing mean squared error over sampled portfolios.

problem_instance.description: SCR proxy learning on a real-world insurance asset-allocation use case.

dataset_specification.description: 26 anonymized asset classes; portfolio vectors sampled by drawing 26 independent uniform random numbers in [0,1] and normalizing to sum to 1; SCR labels computed with an internal tool used in a German insurance company; 40,000 training and 20,000 validation samples.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate normalized random portfolio weights; compute SCR labels using insurer tool.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inspect training/validation error and scatter plot of true vs approximated SCR.

speedup_claims.factor: potential speedup via quantum annealing / QAOA
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical repeated weighted-sum optimization / classical non-convex quadratic optimization
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming future quantum annealing or gate-based quantum hardware with sufficient qubits and low error rates
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical quantum speedup is shown; current hardware is stated to be insufficient for the real-world instance.

experiments.description: Discrete QUBO portfolio optimization experiment using the quadratic SCR proxy, solved with simulated annealing (D-Wave Ocean neal) for a fixed discretization and penalty setting.

algorithm.variant: QUBO solved with simulated annealing via D-Wave Ocean neal

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each of the 26 continuous asset weights x_i is discretized with m=2 bits using the mapping z ≈ sum_k v_k y_k, yielding 52 binary variables total.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min lambda1 f1(T(y)) + lambda2 f2(T(y)) + lambda3 f3,approx(T(y)) + lambdaP (sum_i T(y)_i - 1)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Budget constraint enforced by additive penalty term with lambdaP = 15.

problem_instance.description: 26-asset insurance portfolio optimization with expected return, covariance, and quadratic SCR proxy; Pareto frontier approximated over a grid of weight vectors.

dataset_specification.description: 26 anonymized asset classes from a large insurance company; expected returns and covariance matrix provided in the paper; SCR-related inputs proprietary; weight vectors scanned on a discrete grid.

implementation_details.framework_version: Python 3.11; D-Wave Ocean package; SciPy; pymoo; pytorch
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Quadratic SCR proxy substitution; discretization of portfolio weights into 2-bit grid; scalarization over weight vectors; penalty encoding of budget constraint.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare QUBO solutions to continuous constrained solutions; compute hypervolume indicator and approximation factor.

speedup_claims.factor: potential speedup from quantum annealing / QAOA
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical simulated annealing and classical continuous optimization
speedup_claims.conditions: future generations of quantum annealing hardware or sufficiently capable gate-based quantum computers
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states current hardware is not sufficiently developed for practical use; no quantum hardware speedup is demonstrated. The reported solver is simulated annealing via D-Wave Ocean neal, not actual quantum hardware.
